items.body: ## Description `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B` on vLLM 0.21.0 gives a wrong answer to the simple arithmetic prompt `2 ** 10` when using tensor parallelism. The model outputs `512` or `81` instead of `1024`. When TP=1, the result is correct. This is a **regression** from vLLM 0.19.1, which produces correct results on all configs. ## Reproduction ```python import os; os.environ["VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER"] = "0" from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B" PROMPT = "In Python, what is the output of: 2 ** 10? items.title: [Bug][MoE] DeepEP HT hardcodes per_act_token_quant=False, causing crash/accuracy loss
items.body: ## Bug Description In `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_ht.py:242`, `per_act_token_quant` is hardcoded to `False`: ```python # TODO: support per_act_token_quant, expert_x, expert_x_scale = moe_kernel_quantize_input( expert_x, a1_scale, quant_dtype=quant_config.quant_dtype, per_act_token_quant=False, # <-- should be quant_config.per_act_token_quant block_shape=quant_config.block_shape, ) ``` This causes two issues depending on the quantization method: ### 1. Crash (INT8 models) `CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8MoEMethod` always sets `per_act_token_quant=True`. When using DeepEP HT, the hardcoded `False` is passed to `_int8_quantize()`, which hits: ```python assert per_act_token, "int8 quantization only supports block or channel-wise" ``` ### 2. Silent accuracy degradation (FP8 per-token models) For FP8 models with per-token activation quantization (e.g., `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` with TOKEN strategy, `CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod`, `QuarkFp8MoEMethod` with per-channel input), the hardcoded `False` causes `scaled_fp8_quant(use_per_token_if_dynamic=False)`, computing a single per-tensor scale instead of per-token scales. This can cause significant accuracy loss when token activation magnitudes vary widely (similar root cause to #33011). ## Affected Configurations - **Backend**: `--all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput` - **Quantization methods that set `per_act_token_quant=True`**: - `CompressedTensorsW8A8Int8MoEMethod` (always `True`) → **crash** - `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` (when `strategy == TOKEN`) → accuracy loss - `CompressedTensorsW4A8Fp8MoEMethod` (always `True`) → accuracy loss - `QuarkFp8MoEMethod` (when `input_qscheme == "per_channel"`) → accuracy loss ## Fix One-line change — use `quant_config.per_act_token_quant` instead of `False`: ```python per_act_token_quant=quant_config.per_act_token_quant, ``` This is consistent with how DeepEP LL handles it at `prepare_finalize/deepep_ll.py:217`. ## Note The existing TODO comment at line 237 acknowledges this gap. The docs at `docs/design/moe_kernel_features.md` claim DeepEP HT supports per-activation-token quantization, but the implementation does not match. Found while investigating #33011.

items.title: [Bug] NVFP4: gate_proj / up_proj weight_scale_2 mismatch may cause IMA on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4
items.body: In the `nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4` checkpoint, layer 3 MoE experts have different `weight_scale_2` values for w1 (gate_proj) and w3 (up_proj). From @zhiyucheng's [expert opinion](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4/discussions/1): In ModelOpt, `gate_up_proj` is split into `gate_proj` and `up_proj`. This is because calibrating them separately is more accurate, as the gate and up projections may have different activation distributions. However, when SGLang fuses w1 and w3 into w13, it must collapse the two `weight_scale_2` values into a single scalar alpha, since the FP4 GEMM kernel (eg: flashinfer_trtllm) only accepts one alpha per expert per fused call. Currently in the MoE path, SGLang takes only w1's scale and discards w3's (`modelopt_quant.py:1677-1690`), which introduces dequantization error for the up_proj output. We observed Illegal Memory Access (IMA) errors when running the following configuration on GB300: ```bash # Server python -m sglang.launch_server --model nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 \ --trust-remote-code --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --attention-backend trtllm_mla --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune --sampling-defaults openai \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention # Benchmark python sglang/benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py --host 127.0.0.1 \ --model-path nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 --port 30000 \ --num-clients 256 --max-parallel 256 --num-rounds 20 \ --request-length 512 --output-length 64 ``` We suspect the IMA is caused by the weight_scale_2 mismatch described above. ### Reproduction python -m sglang.launch_server --model nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 \ --trust-remote-code --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --attention-backend trtllm_mla --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm --reasoning-parser kimi_k2 \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k2 --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --disable-flashinfer-autotune --sampling-defaults openai \ --dp-size 4 --tp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention ### Environment gb300

items.title: [Bug][Reasoning] kimi_k3: non-streaming path classifies truncated reasoning as content (inconsistent with streaming path)
items.body: ### Report The `kimi_k3` reasoning parser's non-streaming fallback misclassifies truncated reasoning output as `content`, leaving `reasoning_content` as `null`. The streaming path classifies the exact same output as reasoning, so the two paths disagree. ### Root cause `KimiK3ReasoningParser.extract_reasoning` in `vllm/reasoning/kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py` (main @ f94666b60d): ```python m_open = self._think_open_re.search(model_output) content_start = m_open.end() if m_open is not None else 0 # if there is no think channel at all, everything is content if m_open is None and self._think_close_re.search(model_output) is None: return None, self._content_after_reasoning(model_output, request) ``` The key fact is on the template side: when thinking is enabled, the Kimi K3 chat template ends the prompt with the think **open** marker (` think `) as a generation prefix — the model never generates the open marker itself. So in generated text: - the open marker is (almost) always absent; - the close marker (` think `) is absent whenever the output is truncated (e.g. `max_tokens` smaller than the reasoning length) or generation stops early. That combination falls into the branch above and the whole reasoning text is returned as `content` with `reasoning=None`. Meanwhile, the streaming path in the same file (`extract_reasoning_streaming`) treats any text with no close marker as reasoning: ```python # no close marker anywhere -> still reasoning return DeltaMessage(reasoning=reasoning_delta) ``` So for identical truncated output: `stream=true` returns it as `reasoning_content`, `stream=false` returns it as `content`. This also diverges from the upstream basic parsers (`vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py`), where a missing end token means the whole output stays reasoning (`return model_output, None`). ### Repro Serve Kimi K3 with `--reasoning-parser kimi_k3`, then: ```bash curl http:// /v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "reason step by step: 3 apples cost 12 yuan, how much for 7?"}], "max_tokens": 10, "stream": false }' | jq '.choices[0].message' ``` Returns: ```json { "content": "The user asks to reason step by step about a math problem. items.title: [Bug] DSA top-k v2: tie-overflow selection is not exact — silently returns wrong top-k members (follow-up to #30512 / #30645)
items.body: PR #30512 and #30645 fixed the *crash/validity* symptoms of threshold-bin tie overflow in the fused DSA top-k v2 kernel (all output slots written, no `-1` inside the valid prefix, inf-boundary handling). However the *exactness* gap remains, on `main` as of `ea27e3d`: when more than `kMaxNumTie = 2048` elements fall into the threshold coarse bin, the collect pass keeps whichever 2048 arrive first (`atomicAdd` order — scheduling-dependent, value-independent) and the exact tie-break then runs on that arbitrary subset: ```cpp // topk_impl.cuh (main @ ea27e3d, L595 / L618; same in v0.5.15–v0.5.17) const auto count_eq = atomicAdd(&smem->count_eq, 1); if (count_eq tie.values[count_eq] = {val, idx}; // overflow: value silently dropped ... const auto tie_count = min(equal_count, kMaxNumTie); // select from truncated subset ``` Elements in one coarse bin share only the top fp16 bits — they are *not* fp32-equal — so the dropped candidates can be genuinely larger than the kept ones. The kernel then returns indices that are not the true top-k, with no error or flag, and sparse attention reads wrong KV positions. Note `count_eq` already holds the true bin population, so the overflow is detectable for free; it is just not acted on. This is distinct from the ReLU-degenerate exact-tie case discussed in #30645 (thousands of positions on one exact value — there any subset is acceptable). Our comparison below is against the `torch.topk` **fp32 score multiset**, i.e. exact ties with different indices are accepted; the mismatches are real value losses. ## Evidence on real workloads GLM-5.2-FP8, 8xB200 TP8, official v0.5.17 image, ~1M-token contexts. prs.body: Aria passes shared_experts to FusedMoE but does not set reduce_results=False. So the shared expert all-reduces its output inside LlamaMLP, then FusedMoE all-reduces the total again. items.title: [Bug] Uninitialized rows reach the block-FP8 GEMMs with --moe-a2a-backend deepep (masked by DeepGEMM, NaN with flashinfer)
items.body: Some rows entering the block-FP8 linears hold **uninitialized memory**. Every GEMM backend computes on them and they only differ in what comes out. `deep_gemm` — the auto default on Hopper — saturates the garbage to a finite value, so nothing has ever noticed. `flashinfer` overflows it to NaN, `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT` scans all of `next_token_logits` including those rows, and the scheduler dies during startup: ``` Assertion `NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits` failed. ``` So this is an SGLang initialization bug that the default backend has been masking, not a flashinfer bug. Zeroing the rows makes the crash go away (A/B below), so the cause is established — what I could not find is the allocation that produces them. `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT` is not a debug-only knob: `_pr-test-stage.yml` sets it to `true` for every CI stage except `base-a`. ### Reproduction `main` @ `89f4a80c1`, unmodified, 2x H200, `lmsys/sglang-ci-dsv3-test`. No DP attention, no speculative decoding. **Fails 2/2:** ```bash SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=true python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path lmsys/sglang-ci-dsv3-test --trust-remote-code \ --tp 2 --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_deepgemm ``` The server never becomes healthy; it dies serving the 7-token startup request (`Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 7`). Changing only the last line to `--fp8-gemm-backend deep_gemm` starts fine. Which knobs matter, all with the assertion on: | MoE a2a | DP attn | fp8 backend | result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `deepep` | off | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | **FAIL** | | `deepep` | **on** | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | **FAIL** — DP attention is irrelevant | | `none` | off | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | ok — `deepep` is the trigger | | `deepep` | off | `deep_gemm` | ok | | `deepep` | off | `triton` | ok | ### Root cause **The rows are uninitialized, not miscomputed.** Printing the per-row `amax` of the input at `forward_mha.py::forward_normal_core -> o_proj` (`M=8`, 7 real tokens), rows 0–6 stay in `[0.09, 1.1]` while the last row reads, across calls at the same call site: ``` 6.70e+16 5.09e+35 1.69e+38 2.30e+38 3.10e+38 ``` A value that jumps 22 orders of magnitude call to call is stale memory, not arithmetic. items.title: [Bug]: OffloadingConnector can silently return wrong output at exact chunk boundaries with mamba_cache_mode=all
items.body: `OffloadingConnector` can silently produce different output after a CPU-cache refetch when the prompt length is exactly a multiple of the offloaded Mamba chunk size and `mamba_cache_mode="all"`. `resolve_mamba_align_size()` currently enables hit-window alignment only for `mamba_cache_mode == "align"`: ```python if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align": ... ``` However, `"all"` mode also stores recurrent Mamba states at token/block positions. A prefix lookup is capped at `num_tokens - 1` because the final token must be recomputed for logits. At an exact chunk boundary, without alignment the offload lookup can therefore return `N - 1` tokens while restoring the state stored at boundary `N`. That state already contains token `N`, so recomputing token `N` from it applies the token twice and changes the output without raising an exception. ### Reproduction 1. Create an `LLM` with the configuration above. 2. Use a deterministic token prompt whose length is exactly two offload chunks. In this model/configuration the chunk size was 1408 tokens, so the prompt length was 2816. 3. Generate once with greedy decoding to populate the CPU offload cache. 4. Clear the GPU prefix cache while retaining the connector cache (`reset_connector=False`; on the tested revision the default reset retained it). 5. Generate the identical prompt again. Observed: ```text cold: prompt=2816 cached=0 first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1556] refetch: prompt=2816 cached=2815 first tokens=[18631, 43085, 17091, 47695, 1270] ``` The engine completes normally, but the fifth generated token differs. With the one-line change below, the refetch is rounded back to a valid recurrent-state boundary (`cached=1408` in this setup) and the generated output is bitwise identical to the cold run: ```diff - if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align": + if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode in ("align", "all"): ``` ### Expected behavior A CPU-offloaded prefix hit must never resume from a recurrent state that already includes the token being recomputed. Cold execution and CPU-refetch execution should produce identical greedy output. ### Suggested regression test The existing `test_mamba_align_cpu_offload` already tests exact-boundary and mid-block prompts, but explicitly sets `mamba_cache_mode="align"`. Parameterizing the boundary case with `"all"` should cover this failure. ### Related but separate issue #46453 track

items.body: `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` and `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` let Triton specialize on the 16-byte alignment of their metadata pointers (`cache_indices_ptr`, `query_start_loc_ptr`, `conv_state_indices_ptr`, ...). Three facts make this a problem: 1. **The specialization buys nothing here.** These arrays are read one scalar at a time (a block index, an offset), so the aligned and unaligned binaries run at the same speed. Alignment specialization only pays off for wide vectorized loads (`x_ptr`, `w_ptr`, ... — not these args). 2. **Their alignment flips at runtime.** They are per-step slices of batch metadata, so the address offset depends on the batch layout of that step. 3. **Warmup can never cover the unaligned variant.** Warmup tensors are freshly allocated and therefore always aligned. So the first compile of the unaligned variant is guaranteed to happen *during inference* — this is (part of) the latency spike tracked in #43009, and `jit_monitor` (#45631) duly warns about it. In a multi-node deployment this goes from a latency nuisance to a correctness bug. ### What we hit GRPO RL training, Nemotron-3-Super-120B, 6 vLLM engines on 6 GB200 nodes, with a shared `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` on Lustre (for warm starts). Engines intermittently returned **all-NaN logits from the first prefill token** — only for long prompts, only on some engines, and unreproducible afterwards. items.body: ## System info - transformers 5.12.1, torch 2.10.0+cu130, kernels 0.12.3 - Hub kernel: `kernels-community/deep-gemm`, pinned version 2 (rev `9590415046fa`, internal `__version__` 2.5.0) - GPU: NVIDIA B200 (SM100), CUDA 13.0 - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-FP8` (fine-grained FP8, dynamic activation scheme, fp32 `weight_scale_inv`, `weight_block_size=[128,128]`) ## Bug On SM100, `fp8_linear` prefers the DeepGEMM hub kernel (`integrations/finegrained_fp8.py`, `deepgemm_preferred`). DeepGEMM's only SM100 FP8 GEMM (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d`) consumes UE8M0 (power-of-two) scale factors. transformers satisfies that contract by ceil-rounding the fp32 dequant scales to the next power of two (`integrations/deepgemm.py::_ceil_to_ue8m0` via `_coerce_sf_for_kernel`) — but it never requantizes the data those scales describe: - checkpoint weights were quantized against the original fp32 `weight_scale_inv`; - activations are quantized on the fly with the raw fp32 scale (`_select_fp8_cast_kwargs` returns `use_ue8m0=False` for fp32-scale checkpoints). items.body: With pipeline parallelism (PP > 1) **and** speculative decoding (MTP / EAGLE-style proposer) on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model (`qwen4_exp` in our fork, but the code path is the generic mamba-align postprocess), the mamba "align" postprocess indexes the block table by **batch row** while the request↔row mapping it is given (`idx_mapping`) belongs to the batch from `pp_size` steps ago. When batch composition changes between those steps (a request finishes or a new one is admitted), the recurrent (GDN/conv) state is copied between the **wrong physical mamba blocks** — possibly a live neighbour's, or a block already freed and reassigned. Downstream the GDN recurrence / MoE produce NaN logits or silently wrong tokens. Observed on 8×RTX 3090, TP=2 PP=4, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 1M context with prefix caching: NaN logits in mixed 4-way concurrent runs (nan_lines=5 per run) and a measurable recall drop on a 945K-token RULER-style probe (12/20 and 14/20 correct vs 16/20 with speculation off). `SPEC=0` is unaffected (the align copy only runs on the spec-decode acceptance path); a single request never reorders, so single-stream tests do not trigger it; the fused vs non-fused draft loop only changes timing. ## Where V2 GPU model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`): `execute_model()` starts with `update_pp_decode_requests()`, which pops the `PPHandler` FIFO entry from `pp_size` steps ago and passes its `idx_mapping` to `postprocess_sampled` → `MambaHybridModelState.postprocess_state` → `run_fused_postprocess_align`. The align kernel then used `batch_idx` to index the **gathered, batch-ordered** block table (whose contents are the T−1 batch's), i.e. rows from batch T−pp_size resolved against tables from batch T−1. items.title: OpenAI streaming logprobs and mixed-batch token-id logprobs can return wrong results or crash
items.body: OpenAI-compatible serving has three related logprob / streaming response correctness issues: 1. Chat streaming `top_logprobs` can attach the first token's top-logprobs to every token in a multi-token streaming chunk. 2. Completion streaming can corrupt text when `incremental_streaming_output=True` because already-incremental chunks are sliced by the previous cumulative offset. 3. items.title: [Bug][PD] Bidirectional KV transfer produces incorrect results when reasoning traces are stripped between turns
items.body: Bidirectional KV transfer (PR #32553, RFC #32733) can produce incorrect inference results when used with reasoning models (e.g. DeepSeek-R1) whose thinking traces are stripped from the conversation history between turns. ## Problem When D generates a response with thinking traces, its `kv_transfer_params` records: - `remote_num_tokens = request.num_computed_tokens` — covering `[prompt | thinking_tokens | response_tokens]` - `remote_block_ids` — physical blocks for the entire sequence On the next turn, if the client strips thinking traces before sending, P receives a prompt like `[prompt | response_tokens | new_user_msg]` — the thinking tokens are **missing from the middle**. The block-alignment logic in `_apply_prefix_caching` ([worker.py:2310-2316](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/worker.py#L2310-L2316)) does **suffix trimming**: ```python remote_block_ids[i] = remote_group[-num_local_blocks:] ``` This assumes P's prompt is a strict prefix of D's sequence — true in the normal case, but **broken** when tokens are removed from the middle (for whatever reason, like compacting history or dropping thinking traces). **Result:** P loads KV cache computed for different tokens than its actual input, leading to silently incorrect inference. ## Suggested Fixes **Router-level detection: (currently suggested approach)** A production router can keep the previous turn tokens, indexing by conversation_id. On turn 2, the router can compare prompt tokens. If the prompt is different than expected (traces were stripped), clear the cached kv params and let P fall back to full recomputation. vllm-level fix: We would need to design a thinking tokens-aware solution, possibly block-aligned so that only non-thinking tokens are pulled. This would require significantly more effort and an RFC first.

items.body: I found this issue while testing `dg845/LTX-2.3-Diffusers` with the [verl-omni LTX-2.3 NPU training script](https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/blob/main/examples/flowgrpo_trainer/ltx2/run_ltx2_3_t2av_lora_npu.sh). Further investigation traced the discrepancy to the handling of floating-point attention masks in `_native_npu_attention`. Currently, every non-`None` attention mask is passed to `_maybe_modify_attn_mask_npu`. This helper assumes that the input is a boolean keep mask, converts it to `torch.bool`, and then inverts it because PyTorch SDPA and `npu_fusion_attention` use opposite boolean-mask polarities: - PyTorch SDPA: `True` means attend. - `npu_fusion_attention`: `True` means discard. items.body: On **NVIDIA Hopper (sm_90, e.g. H20/H100)**, serving a Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct LoRA adapter with vLLM produces **completely garbled output** (e.g. repeated `!!!!!!`, or incoherent mixed-language/code-like tokens). The **base model without LoRA is perfectly fine**. I traced this to the LoRA **`lora_expand`** Triton kernel producing **NaN**. `lora_shrink` is fine. The trigger is the default expand kernel config **`block_n = 128`** (single-slice path); forcing **`block_n = 32`** makes the kernel numerically correct and the garbling disappears. items.title: [Bug]: --kv-cache-dtype fp8 produces garbage output on MLA models (GLM-4.7-Flash) at multi-turn
items.body: FP8 KV cache produces corrupted output on MLA models when the conversation exceeds a single turn. Single-turn responses are coherent, multi-turn with system prompts degrades to garbage. ### Reproduction ```bash vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 8192 ``` Single turn (works fine): ```json {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in Finnish"}]} → coherent response about "Hei" / "Terve" ``` Multi-turn with system prompt (broken): ```json {"messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful sales assistant for a SaaS product."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What pricing plans do you offer?"} ]} → "...a S componentes_obs Worce!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!" ``` ### Benchmark data Tested across 20 multi-turn conversation scenarios with Llama-3.3-70B judge (score 1-5): | Model | KV Cache | Avg Score | |-------|----------|-----------| | GLM-4.7-Flash BF16 | FP16 (baseline) | 4.61 | | GLM-4.7-Flash BF16 | **FP8** | **1.07** | | Qwen3-235B AWQ | FP16 (baseline) | 4.74 | | Qwen3-235B AWQ | FP8 | 4.71 | FP8 works fine on standard FlashAttention models (Qwen3-235B). Only MLA models are affected. ### Analysis The vLLM log shows: `"Using fp8 data type to store kv cache. It reduces the GPU memory footprint and boosts the performance. Meanwhile, it may cause accuracy drop without a proper scaling factor."` The FLASHMLA backend appears to apply FP8 quantization to MLA's latent vectors (`kv_c_normed`) without calibrated per-tensor scaling. As the KV cache grows with conversation turns, quantization error compounds. For comparison, TurboQuant+ (PolarQuant) compression on the same model scores 4.63/5 across the same scenarios, because it normalizes each vector independently before quantization, preventing error accumulation. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues) for "fp8 MLA" and "fp8 kv cache MLA" and found no duplicates.

items.body: SGLang can show lower benchmark accuracy than vLLM for DeepSeek-V4-Flash W4A8 on Blackwell / SM100. This issue uses GPQA Diamond as the concrete reproducer, but the problem is not GPQA-specific. The suspected cause is the FP8 `wo_a` activation scale layout passed to `deep_gemm.fp8_einsum` in `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`. Since this path can change model logits during inference, the bug causes low accuracy across downstream evaluations. We have confirmed this on GPQA, AIME25, and SWE-Bench; after applying the layout fix, accuracy recovered on these evaluations. Fix PR: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29036 ## Suspected Root Cause The current FP8 `wo_a` path quantizes `o: [T, G, D]` by flattening it into `[T * G, D]`, then views the packed UE8M0 scales back as `[T, G, -1]`. On the SM100 DeepGEMM FP8 einsum path, this can mismatch activation scales with groups and cause early logit divergence. PR #29036 changes the quantization/scale layout to preserve group-major semantics. ## Impact This is an inference correctness issue, not only a GPQA-specific regression. The incorrect FP8 `wo_a` scale layout introduces logit divergence in the DeepGEMM path, so benchmarks and workloads that depend on stable reasoning, code generation, or action generation can be affected. GPQA is used here because it is a small and repeatable benchmark where we observed a clear accuracy gap and recovery after the layout fix. We have also reproduced low-accuracy symptoms on AIME25 and SWE-Bench, and after applying the same layout fix, accuracy recovered on those evaluations as well. Confirmed affected evaluations include: - GPQA - AIME25 - SWE-Bench Other math, reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks may also be affected by the same inference correctness issue. ## Environment - Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash W4A8 - Hardware: Blackwell / SM100 - SGLang baseline: `v0.5.12.post1` - Reproducer dataset: GPQA Diamond, 198 examples ## Server Command Baseline and patched SGLang used the same server arguments. items.title: [Bug] PD disaggregation: aborted prefill requests (input too long) cause decode to generate garbage from incomplete KV cache
items.body: # Bug Description In PD disaggregation mode, when a request's input length exceeds max_req_input_len (but is under context_len), the prefill side aborts via set_finish_with_abort, which truncates origin_input_ids to 1 token. However, the aborted request still enters the prefill queue, and send_kv_chunk transfers only 1 token of KV cache to the decode side. The decode side, which allocated space for the full prompt length, starts decoding from incomplete/uninitialized KV cache, producing garbage output. # Root Cause 1. validate_input_length fails (input > max_req_input_len), allow_auto_truncate=False 2. set_finish_with_abort replaces origin_input_ids with array("q", [0]) (1 token placeholder) 3. Aborted request still enters prefill queue via _add_request_to_queue 4. send_kv_chunk computes end_idx = min(fill_len, len(origin_input_ids)) = min(1, 1) = 1, only sends 1 token of KV cache 5. Decode side allocates space for full prompt length (284937) but only receives 1 token of KV data 6. Decode starts from 284936 uninitialized KV cache slots → garbage output Additionally, process_disagg_prefill_inflight_queue overwrites FINISH_ABORT with FINISH_LENGTH(length=0) when KVPoll.Success is received for the 1-token transfer. # Key Parameters max_total_num_tokens = 284928 (determined by mem_fraction_static) max_req_len = min(context_len, max_total_num_tokens) = 284928 max_req_input_len = max_req_len - page_size - 1 = 284922 #Request with 284937 tokens > 284922 → triggers abort # Fix The fix ensures that aborted prefill requests do not transfer KV cache and instead notify the decode side to abort as well: ```python diff --git a/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/base/conn.py b/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/base/conn.py index a7bf9904a2..a273fc0bbf 100644 --- a/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/base/conn.py +++ b/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/base/conn.py @@ -95,7 +95,6 @@ class BaseKVManager(ABC): class BaseKVSender(ABC): - @abstractmethod def __init__( self, @@ -151,7 +150,6 @@ class BaseKVSender(ABC): class BaseKVReceiver(ABC): - @abstractmethod def __init__( self, @@ -209,6 +207,13 @@ class BaseKVReceiver(ABC): """ pass + def notify_decode_abort(self): + """ + Notify the decode side that this request was aborted on prefill side. + The decode side should also abort the request. + """ + pass + class BaseKVBootstrapServer(ABC): @abstractmethod diff --git a/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py b/python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py index f025bbd7a

prs.title: fix(pd): propagate pre-queue aborts to decode
prs.body: ## Motivation Fixes #30233. In PD disaggregation, scheduler validation can reject a request after decode has already allocated KV for the original prompt. `Req.set_finish_with_abort()` replaces `origin_input_ids` with a one-token placeholder, but the rejected request previously still entered the normal PD queues. That can make prefill transfer a one-token handoff while decode waits for or decodes from KV allocated for the original prompt. The client may receive garbage output, a transfer timeout, or a generic 500 instead of the original 400. ## Modifications ### Stop rejected requests before PD queue admission - PREFILL and DECODE modes finish already-aborted requests before normal bootstrap

items.title: FineGrainedFP8: modules_to_not_convert never matches on text-only loads of multimodal checkpoints (silent quality corruption)
items.body: **Summary.** `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` ships `quantization_config.modules_to_not_convert` with multimodal-wrapper paths (`model.language_model.layers...`). items.body: The HF checkpoint config for `meituan-longcat/LongCat-2.0-FP8` uses these keys for the n-gram over-embedding: - `oe_vocab_size_ratio` - `oe_neighbor_num` - `oe_split_num` while `LongcatFlashConfig` (from the #30042 branch) reads: - `ngram_vocab_size_ratio` - `emb_neighbor_num` - `emb_split_num` Because none of the expected keys are present, `use_ngram_embedding` resolves to `False` and **all 32 `model.ngram_embeddings.*` weights are silently dropped at load time** — the only trace is a "not found in params_dict" warning buried in the loader logs. items.title: [Bug]: kv_load_failure_policy="recompute" gives wrong output when a KV connector rejects a synchronous load (V2 runner)
items.body: ### Description With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, when a KV connector promises externally cached prefix tokens and the load is then rejected, the request is recomputed but its output is wrong. It does not match a clean run with no connector, even though the rejected load moved no data. Recovery reports success (`Recovered from KV load failure: 1 request(s) rescheduled`), but the decoded result is garbage under synchronous scheduling and an offset continuation under asynchronous scheduling. This also breaks the invariant that the `examples/disaggregated/kv_load_failure_recovery_offline` example checks, which is a `cmp -s` of the recovered output against the baseline. That example runs Llama-3.2-1B, which uses the V2 runner, but it is an example script that is not run in CI, so the regression went unnoticed. ### Setup - vLLM `0.25.1`. The affected code is byte-identical on `main`. - The V2 GPU model runner, which is the default for any non-MoE generative model (Qwen3, Llama-3.2, and similar). The startup log shows `Using V2 Model Runner`. - Single GPU, TP=1, FlashAttention-2, `--enforce-eager`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. - A custom `KVConnectorBase_V1` (`kv_role="kv_both"`) doing a synchronous load (`get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns `load_async=False`), with `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`. prs.body: ## Purpose Fixes #49250. When a synchronous external KV load is rejected under `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, scheduler state is rewound but Model Runner V2 can retain state written by discarded in-flight frames. prs.title: [KERNELS] Pad Hopper MX scale K-tail storage
prs.body: Addresses #10772 ## Why `HopperMXScaleLayout` pads the scale-K dimension to a multiple of 2, but the Hopper matmul kernels read scale storage for a full `BLOCK_K` tile at a time. items.body: Both ancestral schedulers produce **all-NaN output** when configured with `beta_schedule="squaredcos_cap_v2"` at low step counts (the standard ancestral fast-sampling regime, ~4–10 steps): - `EulerAncestralDiscreteScheduler`: `step(...).prev_sample` comes back entirely NaN. - `KDPM2AncestralDiscreteScheduler`: NaN appears even earlier — it leaks into `self.timesteps` during `set_timesteps(...)`. Root cause (same in both files): ```python sigma_up = (sigma_to**2 * (sigma_from**2 - sigma_to**2) / sigma_from**2) ** 0.5 sigma_down = (sigma_to**2 - sigma_up**2) ** 0.5 ``` Mathematically `sigma_up = 0`. But `squaredcos_cap_v2` drives the terminal `alphas_cumprod` to ~0, giving a huge sigma dynamic range (`sigma[0] ≈ 2.0e4`). In **float32**, when `sigma_from >> sigma_to`, rounding makes `sigma_up` come out *fractionally larger* than `sigma_to`, so `sigma_to**2 - sigma_up**2` becomes slightly negative → `sqrt` → `NaN`, which then propagates into the sample. This is `squaredcos_cap_v2` + low steps specifically; `linear` / `scaled_linear` keep the radicand comfortably positive and are unaffected. `squaredcos_cap_v2` is listed as a supported `beta_schedule` in the `EulerAncestralDiscreteScheduler` docstring. **Affected files (one pattern, two instances — filing as a single issue per the AI-agent contribution guide's "fix patterns, not one-offs"):** - `src/diffusers/schedulers/scheduling_euler_ancestral_discrete.py` — inside `step()` - `src/diffusers/schedulers/scheduling_k_dpm_2_ancestral_discrete.py` — inside `set_timesteps()` (precomputed, so the NaN reaches `self.timesteps`) The non-ancestral `KDPM2DiscreteScheduler` carries the same dead value in `sigmas_interpol[0]` but never reads it, so it is not affected. items.title: [Bug]: Composite VLM wrapper (Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration) resolves tie_word_embeddings from the wrong (top-level) config, silently discarding a real lm_head.weight and producing coherent-vocabulary-but-incoherent output
items.body: ## Summary For a `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` checkpoint (Ministral-3 family) in HF format, vLLM produces deterministic gibberish (grammatically-plausible, real-vocabulary, multi-language tokens with no coherent meaning) regardless of prompt, while plain `transformers.generate()` on the identical checkpoint is fully coherent. No error or warning is raised at load time. Root cause: `transformers`' own `Mistral3Config.__init__` (the top-level composite-wrapper config class) hardcodes `tie_word_embeddings: bool = True` as its own signature default and never reads/syncs it from `text_config` -- while `Ministral3Config` (the nested `text_config` class actually used for the language model) independently defaults to `tie_word_embeddings=False`. These are two different classes with two different hardcoded defaults, so any checkpoint whose `config.json` doesn't explicitly pin both fields (e.g. the pristine base model itself) loads with a latent conflict between them -- before any merge/export/fine-tuning is involved. `transformers`' own weight-tying logic uses `text_config` (confirmed: `transformers.generate()` is coherent, and the checkpoint's `lm_head.weight`/`embed_tokens.weight` are verifiably distinct tensors, see below), so the top-level field is functionally vestigial there and the mismatch is invisible to `transformers` itself. vLLM appears to resolve tying from the top-level field instead, silently discards the checkpoint's real, correctly-trained `lm_head.weight`, and computes output logits through `embed_tokens.weight` instead -- explaining the exact symptom (valid vocabulary, incoherent output) with no load-time error, since a redundant `lm_head` tensor under an assumed-tied model is normally dropped silently by vLLM's weight loader rather than flagged. ## Environment - vLLM 0.25.1 - Checkpoint: HF-format LoRA-merge of `mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Base-2512` (`architectures: ["Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration"]`, `model_type: "mistral3"`, nested `text_config.model_type: "ministral3"`) - Reproduced under both vLLM's native `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration` implementation and `model_impl="transformers"` (the generic Transformers-modeling-backend fallback) -- **identical** gibberish output under both, including in `enforce_eager=True` mode (CUDA graphs ruled out). This points to the bug being in something vLLM's engine does identically across both model-implementation backends (weight-tying resolution), not in either backend's own forward-pass/kernel c

prs.title: [MoE][Offload] Run MoE models exceeding VRAM via expert CPU offloading with GPU cache (--moe-expert-cache-size)
prs.body: ## Purpose `CachedWeightProvider` — MoE expert CPU offloading with GPU LFRU cache, addressing [RFC #38256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38256). Expert weights live in CPU pinned memory; a fixed-size GPU cache holds the hottest N experts per layer using LFRU (frequency-weighted LRU) eviction. LFRU prevents early layers from monopolizing the cache — a known problem with pure LRU in sequential MoE execution. Models that exceed GPU VRAM can now run on smaller hardware. **No runner bypass** — all paths go through `quant_method.apply()`. EP dispatch, DP chunking, and shared expert overlap work unchanged. **References:** [RFC #38256](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38256)
